children: HONG KONG, HONG KONG, November 22nd, 2026, Chainwire
Following the activation of native staking rewards,
holders can now reinvest rewards automatically while keeping a native staking position.

Pharos Network, the value discovery layer for the agentic economy and RealFi (Real-World Finance), today announced the launch of the Native Staking Workbench through Anvita Mate, an AI-powered interactive Workbench in the Pharos ecosystem. With a one-time operator authorization,
holders can delegate to validators and have their native staking rewards compounded automatically, without triggering each operation manually.

Native staking has been live on Pharos since its Mainnet launch, and staking rewards were recently activated after 6 months of Mainnet launch, allowing eligible delegators to earn protocol rewards in proportion to their stake. On Pharos, rewards accrue each epoch but are added to the staked principal only when the staking contract's compound function is called. The Native Staking Workbench automates this step.
How It Works

The workbench is built into the existing Anvita Mate client and is accessible via the Pharos Staking website. Once a user grants operator authorization, Anvita Mate's backend calls the compound function every epoch (approximately every four hours). This adds eligible rewards back to the user's native staking position, so they take part in later reward distributions. Staked
remains tied to the user's wallet and native position. The workbench issues no separate coin and does not alter the protocol's reward issuance rules. No additional user fee applies at launch.
Where Rewards Come From
Pharos staking rewards come from two sources: protocol inflation and network transaction fees. Under current parameters, annual inflation is 5%. Based on the initial supply of 1 billion
, that is approximately 50 million
per year, with rewards distributed each epoch according to on-chain rules. The 5% inflation rate is a protocol parameter and should not be read as the APR an individual holder receives.

Actual returns depend on the effective staking ratio, validator performance and commission, transaction-fee rewards, and whether rewards are reinvested. Without compounding, accumulated rewards do not increase the principal used to calculate future rewards. With compounding, they do, so later rewards accrue on a larger position. The resulting APY therefore reflects the underlying APR, compounding frequency, fees, and network conditions. Staking rewards are variable and not guaranteed, and any APR or APY figures are illustrative only.
Two Ways to Stake

holders can choose between native staking and liquid staking. With native staking through Anvita Mate, users keep a direct native position and automate reward reinvestment. With Faroo's liquid staking, users receive stPROS, a liquid staking token whose exchange rate against PROS reflects accumulated rewards. stPROS can be used across supported DeFi applications, subject to associated risks. The two options serve different liquidity needs and preferences.

As Pharos builds out its RealFi infrastructure, native staking remains central to network security and tokenholder participation. Auto-compounding builds on this protocol-level foundation to make reinvestment more convenient. Together with publicly documented staking economics, it aims to make Pharos staking more accessible, transparent, and usable.
holders can explore native staking with auto-compounding through Anvita Mate at https://port.pharos.xyz/stake.
